prose.title: CBP Did Nothing for Three Months, Then Spent to the Last Dollar
prose.dek: Derrick Whitman started April with {{f.team.0002.active_roster_opening}} active players and made no move until the auction, then spent {{f.team.0002.faa_spend}} on Jonathan Taylor, Kyle Pitts and the Tony Pollard that C-Town let go. He has {{f.team.0002.cap_current_room}} of cap room left, and the preseason simulation ranks CBP {{f.team.0002.power_rank|ord}}.

paragraphs: April was nearly empty: {{f.team.0002.active_roster_opening}} active players and {{f.team.0002.cap_opening}} in salary. Nico Collins was the one top-twelve starter, and Jordan Love, Emeka Egbuka and Garrett Wilson were solid. The {{f.team.0002.holes_opening}} holes were Keaton Mitchell at running back, nobody at all at the second running back spot, Cole Kmet at tight end, Ricky Pearsall in a flex and Spencer Rattler in the superflex.

Then Whitman did nothing, which is how he works: the roster business happens in silence. No trade, no cut, no extension before the rookie draft, and his one expiring rookie deal, A.T. Perry's, simply ran out.

t.0002.slot_bridge.title: April: who held each priced slot

paragraphs: The draft was the whole pre-auction offseason. Whitman made {{f.team.0002.rookie_picks_count}} picks, two in the first round: Kenyon Sadiq at 1.08, a slot where history finds a usable player a little under half the time, and Eli Stowers at 1.12, where it almost never has. Jonah Coleman at 2.01, Ted Hurst, Cade Klubnik and a defender, Keyshaun Elliott, followed. Sadiq and Coleman are already on the redraft board, both replacement-level for now.

No Expired Rookie Auction buys, no tags, no cuts, no trades. He went into the auction with {{f.team.0002.active_roster_preauction}} active players and {{f.team.0002.cap_preauction}} committed: plenty of room, and plenty of rebuilding to do with it.

CBP spent {{f.team.0002.faa_spend}} at the Free Agent Auction on {{f.team.0002.faa_lots_won}} players, and made a little more room first. On the auction's opening weekend Jordan Love was extended one more year, {{f.team.0002.contract_14782_next_salary}} for 2027, and restructured the same day, back-loaded to {{f.team.0002.contract_14782_salary_2}} this year and {{f.team.0002.contract_14782_next_salary_2}} next. Then Whitman bought a backfield: Jonathan Taylor for {{f.team.0002.faa_14802_price}}, D'Andre Swift for {{f.team.0002.faa_14797_price}} and Tony Pollard, cut by C-Town on lock day, for {{f.team.0002.faa_14085_price}} after thirteen bids. Kyle Pitts cost {{f.team.0002.faa_15329_price}}.

What it bought was real: Taylor, an Elite RB1; Pitts, a High-end TE1 and the Very good buy; Swift, the Good one; and Pollard, who starts. Aaron Jones and Michael Pittman are depth. Only C-Town's offense improved more at the auction; the league table ranks CBP {{f.team.0002.faa_off_rank|ord}} of {{f.league.teams}}.

The contracts that followed ran him to the cap. Pitts signed front-loaded, {{f.team.0002.contract_15329_salary}} this year and {{f.team.0002.contract_15329_next_salary}} in 2027. In late August Nico Collins's deal was restructured to {{f.team.0002.rt_15290_salary}} this year and put back {{f.team.0002.rt_15290_days}} days later, a temporary {{f.team.0002.restructure_room_freed}} of room, and in between Whitman took Jayden Reed, three depth players and {{f.team.0002.trade_blind_bid_cash}} of blind-bid money from Blake Bombers for Pearsall, Coleman and a 2027 fourth, a {{f.team.0002.trade1_grade}} from the trade bot. He cut Kmet at no cost, claimed Calvin Ridley and Xavier Hutchinson off waivers, and sits at {{f.team.0002.cap_current_room}} of room.

The lineup it built has {{f.team.0002.studs_today}} top-twelve starters, Taylor, Collins and Pitts, five solid ones around them, and {{f.team.0002.holes_today}} hole, Pollard in a flex. Quarterback is the soft spot: Tyler Shough and Love both grade as a Mid QB2, and his quarterbacks rank {{f.team.0002.qb_rank|ord}} in the league. Graded on MFL's projections the defense is thin, Foyesade Oluokun the only defender above replacement level.
No starter is hurt. The injury list is all bench and taxi: Keaton Mitchell and Eli Stowers are questionable, and Isiah Pacheco and Dillon Gabriel are on injured reserve into October.

t.0002.moves_s3.title: From the auction to week one

captions.t.0002.faa_value: Ranked by how much each owner's starting offense improved between the auction lock and the close; a buy that never makes the lineup adds nothing. What it bought grades each quarterback, back, receiver and tight end at his position: Elite is the top three, Very good the rest of the top twelve, Good the next twelve at quarterback, back and receiver (every team starts two, counting the superflex), Starter anyone else the league's lineups would start, and Depth the rest.

paragraphs: Whitman's teams have had the league's best all-play record {{f.team.0002.hist_ap_titles}} times, in {{f.team.0002.hist_ap_title_years}}, and won {{f.team.0002.hist_div_titles}} division titles, but the championship count is one, in {{f.team.0002.hist_title_years}}, with a runner-up finish in {{f.team.0002.hist_runner_up_years}}. His career all-play record is {{f.team.0002.hist_allplay_pct}}.

This year's division is one he built. Whitman sat {{f.league.div_draft_captain_0002|ord}} among the four captains, took Gride {{f.league.div_draft_pick_0003|ord}} overall and came back for Blake Bombers {{f.league.div_draft_pick_0010|ord}}, and he has made a point of calling LEGION OF BOOM his division, not ours, because he put it together. The simulation is less sure it is his: Blake Bombers are the favorite at {{f.league.p_division_0010}}, CBP is at {{f.team.0002.sim_p_division}} with {{f.team.0002.sim_p_playoffs}} playoff odds, and Gride is at {{f.league.p_division_0003}}.

The division weeks are {{f.team.0002.div_weeks}}, and one of them is a problem. Week eight costs him Shough and Collins, while Gride and Blake Bombers lose three starters each, George Kittle and Brock Purdy among Blake's. But week eleven takes six CBP starters at once, Pitts, Love and four defenders, against four apiece for his rivals. Week fourteen, the last of the regular season, has no byes at all in the division. Across the five weeks he loses {{f.team.0002.div_week_own_byes}} starters to byes and his rivals {{f.team.0002.div_week_rival_byes}}.

The next three years CBP style no commas. 2027 the young guys grow up and CBP does not say a word about it until somebody else brings it up and then CBP says a lot. 2028 playoffs and the quarterback problem gets solved in silence at an auction. 2029 the division title in the division he put together himself and a thank you to the whole league because we are all friends here and then quiet for a year.
Week one is a division week and has barely touched CBP: with {{f.league.wk_teams_final}} NFL teams done, Leonard Williams had a sack and CBP has {{f.team.0002.wk_points_final}} points in the bank.
